utterances.text: But it wasn't the practice for Mr. Martic to warn you, then? For your superiors to warn you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Martic drew our attention to that because of Bozo Ceko who had spent three months in Zagreb in prison. That's why he drew our attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Knezevic? Have I pronounced your name properly? Have I done you enough justice in pronouncing your name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Knezevic, how many Dragan Knezevics were there at Golubic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were Knezevics in all places in Srmik [phoen], in Civljani, in Cetina, all over the place. So I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you? We don't have much time. Listen to my question. How many Dragan Knezevics were there in Golubic, at the camp, where you were -- when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Believe me that I don't know. It may have been just me. There may have been another one. I really don't know because there were between 250 and 300 people there so that I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not aware of any other Dragan Knezevic who was ever at Golubic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I know that there was a Dragan Knezevic from Strmica; now, whether he was there at that time, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Knezevic, please let's not talk about Strmica. I'm talking about Golubic. At Golubic, to your knowledge, you were the only Dragan Knezevic, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: It is possible but I cannot assert that, namely it could have been just me and there may have been some others. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to the question, please. We haven't got much time. When you say it's possible, what is possible? My question to you is, to your knowledge, you should know, you either know that there was another or you don't know. To your knowledge, you were the only Dragan Knezevic at Golubic. To your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't know if -- okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I only know about me. I don't know about any others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. To your knowledge, you know only of yourself. That's the question I'm asking you, sir. I don't know why it's so difficult about answering that question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said that Kijevo was a Croat Alamo. What is an Alamo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: The Croatian media actually extolled Kijevo, calling it the Croatian Alamo, and Mr. Franjo Tudjman said himself that when Kijevo fell, Croatia would fall, and I don't know what exactly he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is what is an Alamo.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Alamo is a city in the United States. It is a symbol of the United States. It is a symbol of their fight for freedom against the Indians. I'm not quite sure. I'm not that familiar with their history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's against the Mexicans, not the Indians, the fight against the Mexicans. And they lost the Alamo, in San Antonio.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: As I said I'm not very familiar with the history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: If you maybe had seen this or movie but just, it is not against the Indians --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who was Heni, the person who secretly filmed the footage? You suggested he probably filmed the [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention Heni Erceg, she was a correspondent for the Slobodna Dalmatia, a Croatian lady journalist who worked in Split for the Slobodna Dalmacija. I had heard of her. I had heard her name referred to. She was a quite well known journalist in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, did I hear you correctly to say that she is the probably the one who filmed this film -- this footage of Mr. Martic secretly? Or did I mishear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I heard that from my colleague, Zarko, Rados, that she had filmed it. I wasn't there then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you knew about there footage before you came to court today. Because you were told it was filmed by -- you were told by Zarko Rados that she filmed it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Just one minute, Your Honours. I didn't know that that was this particular footage. I knew of the existence of some video footage. I didn't know that it was this particular one which I saw for the first time today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you can't say that this footage was done by Heni. You can't say it was done secretly. If you don't know, you have no basis for talking about Heni and secretly footing -- filming this footage. You were just speculating. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that I had heard about this from my colleague Zarko Rados, who had been there. I hadn't seen it myself. Had I seen it myself, I would have described it differently. I cannot claim that it was done secretly or publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please listen to the question. You were told by Ratko -- Zarko Rados.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: About secret filming of a footage of some sort. You don't know what film was the footage. Therefore when you say maybe this is the one you are actually speculating. You are not -- you can't -- you have no basis for saying what you heard from him relates to this film that we saw today.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that Mr. Martic ordered you to make sure that nothing became of the prisoners that were being taken to Knin. He said that to you because he was your superior, he was in control, am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you also referred in answer to question by Judge Nosworthy, that the people, the police who went to the field wore camouflage uniform and the police in town wore the normal type uniform. Remember that? Just a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was the colour of the normal-type uniform that was worn by the police in town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: The shirt -- the jacket was light blue, and there was -- actually the shirt was light blue and the jacket was dark blue and the trousers were greyish blue. That is the summer uniform. And then the winter uniform was greyish blue and it also had a light blue shirt and a tie was worn with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say light blue are you talking of something that looks like the screen of your -- the screen in front of you? The screen of this monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Just like this colour at the very top of the monitor. That blue. At the very top of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Unfortunately, I don't see your screen and I've got -- my two screens show different colour blue. So I'll leave it at that but you say that -- do you see any blue in this room that you can --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: The colour of Mr. Martic's shirt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The colour of Mr. Martic's shirt. Maybe you must get Mr. Martic as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: What can I do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My last question to you: On what basis do you say broadcasting this speech that we saw on the clip here would fan the flames of national passions? You said so in answer to a question by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, what speech are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic asked you about the clip that we saw here where Mr. Martic was speaking. You remember that clip? The footage that we saw today. Right. And he asked you what company, television, this was that broadcast it and you said it must have been a Croatian television. He asked you what would be the effect of broadcasting that kind of -- and what was the purpose of the television company broadcasting and you said the purpose that -- the only purpose that you could see was to fan the flames of national passions. You remember that? Now, you seem to be lost. Let me take you back to your words.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I do remember that, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You remember that. My question to you is: On what basis do you say, why do you say, broadcasting that would fan the flames of national passions? Broadcasting never fans national passions. Broadcasts are broadcasts. Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand your question fully, and you are suggesting the answer to me, and I will give you an answer right now. The broadcasting of this footage that we have seen here on this screen could have had a countereffect and it did have a countereffect among Croatian people, namely they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you is why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I say it because I, as a member of the interior forces, the regular organ of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, remained without everything that I had in Croatia, and remained virtually without anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry, you're not answering my question. You're answering another question. My question is very simple. Why would broadcasting that footage fan national passions? Just tell me that, please. Just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll be frank. Someone needed that and who it served somebody's interests and it was others who made the decisions that I don't know whose purposes it served.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're still not answering my question. I'm sorry, I'm asking you why you say that broadcasting that clip would fan national passions. Why would broadcasting fan national passions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Because Mr. Martic stated that he didn't want the chequer-board flag as an emblem, that he didn't want the police to be called the redarstvenici in the police station at Knin, or in what was referred to as the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, which was in existence at that time because those were emblems that irritated. And he didn't want them because they were reminiscent of a dark past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So in fact, you're now talking about what Mr. Martic said not the broadcasting so it was because of what was being said that you think national passions would have been fanned. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends, depends on whom you show it to. If you show it to the Croatian public, it will certainly be inflammatory. If shown to the Serbian public --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't say that to Mr. Milovancevic. You said it would fan national passions. You didn't say, it depends on what. I'm asking you, you say so because of what was being said in that statement, isn't it so? That's what fanned the national passion. What was said in that statement, what fanned the national passion, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Martic stated that he didn't want the Croatian authorities there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please answer my question. We are way past the time we should knock off. I'm not asking you what Martic said. I'm asking you what fanned national passions was the content of the statement. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: What was stated in the statement, which we have seen here, it is a very complex issue and I cannot give you a simple answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, I asked you a very simple question in the beginning. I said, why would the broadcasting fan the passions, because that's what you said in your answer. And do you know what you said amongst other things? You said because Mr. Martic mentions the chequer-board, mentions these things and that thing, and he doesn't like those things. That's why I've moved from broadcasting to the content. So based on what you said, that it is because of what Mr. Martic said so you are actually agreeing with me that it is the content of the speech that fans the passions. Is that not so? It's a very simple question. Can you just say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: That this -- Martic's statement actually led to the fanning of passions, no, no. Because seeing that there was a generally negative -- the emotions were running high and were generally negatively charged, this can be characterised in a number of ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if you say that it's not the statement that is fanning the passions, how does broadcasting fan the passions? Because you never answered that question. Tell me now: Why is broadcasting fanning passions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it depends on when it is broadcast, to what audience it is broadcast, before whom it is broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you is simple, sir: Why is the act of broadcasting fanning passions. The statement is clean. There is nothing that fans passions you've just told us. Why is the act of broadcasting fanning passions, it doesn't matter to whom. Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I have sufficiently responded to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not crazy. If you had sufficiently responded I would have stopped asking you questions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to say this. It depends on how you interpret or convey someone's statements and at what particular moment it is broadcast. This is what it depends on the most. Perhaps it would not have had an effect and then again it might have had a tremendous effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why didn't you say to Mr. Milovancevic when he asked you the question, it depends? You just said it fans the passions. You didn't say it depends on who you say it to or how you broadcast it. Why didn't you say to him, it depends? Why do you give me a different answer from the one you gave Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you a different answer but the gentlemen didn't ask me about the details and you're asking me about the details. That is why I answered in such extensive fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the details. I'm asking you why broadcasting that statement fans passions. You said to Mr. Milovancevic broadcasting it fans passions. I'm asking you why. And you didn't say to Mr. Milovancevic, oh, it depends. Why do you say "it depends" to me? That's a different answer you're giving me.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Milovancevic asked me, and I should quote him, "Would the broadcasting of such a statement fan national passions? Or not?" And I said, "Yes, it would." He didn't ask me anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm just asking you one question. Why would that fan national passions. If you answer me that, then we go home.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Well it goes without saying, because of the statement itself. But I should like to add it depends where it is broadcast and before what audience, to what audience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What fans national passions is the statement. It's not the broadcasting, it's what you're saying from what you just told me now. It is the statement that fans passions, not the broadcasting. If that broad statement was not made, there would have been no fanning of passions. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. It has taken -- it was like extracting a tooth. Okay. There can obviously be no re-examination --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: Almost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are going to have to adjourn until next week because -- okay. Yes, Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I was just going to say I don't have any follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. Milovancevic has so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't. Thank you very much. In that event, sir, thank you very much for coming to court. This brings us to the end of your testimony. On behalf of the Chamber, once again I thank you. You are now excused. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: What the interpreter could hear was, "Can I just say hello to Mr. Martic?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are in court, please. Just go out, please. No, just go out, you'll talk to -- sorry. Mr. Milovancevic we have that housekeeping matter that you were going to talk to your team about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this moment, I can only tell you that we shall endeavour to do that as urgently as possible. If the period should prove to be too short, we shall postpone that witness for somewhat later so that we shall be mindful of the OTP's needs to have sufficient time to acquaints themselves with the statement and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said that that witness is coming to testify only on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours, certainly not before that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have other witnesses coming on Monday before Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for Monday and Tuesday, we have no witnesses. In view of the instruction that we have been issued from you, we are preparing a wholly new schedule of our witnesses and we are seeking to finish the case within the deadline set by you so that we are now selecting our witnesses and rescheduling our witnesses. We will be informing you what witnesses will be appearing, of course, always trying to fully abide by the deadline that you have set for us. We shall, in fact, honour that deadline. There is no question mark about it, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But you're saying Monday and Tuesday we have no witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we don't have any witnesses secured at this point in time. We have, in fact, informed you that we have abandoned some witnesses and as regards the other witnesses, we are reassessing everything which still needs to be presented in our case, including expert reports, expert findings, and we shall be informing of on all this on Monday the minute we have finish our preparations. We please ask to you bear with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I may, I'm grateful for the indications from Mr. Milovancevic but it seems that Wednesday also would be -- there would be nothing scheduled for Wednesday because the next witness that -- the only witness that we've been told about is -- we have been told is coming on Thursday at the earliest. We have been told about no other witnesses. So I assume that Wednesday is also off, and if we could get some clarification on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, can you clarify us, please? And while your learned friend is grateful for the indication, I regret that we get the indication so late. Yes, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we were confronted with the position of the Trial Chamber a few days ago and we are seeking to honour your instructions. We had in mind certain witnesses but we were unfortunate - and I'm not going to refer to any names - that some of our witnesses had to be abandoned because of some health problems, so that we are seeking to rearrange the other witnesses that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, listen to the point and the question at issue. The question at issue is, we want you to confirm: Is Wednesday also off? Just yes or no. You told us a whole lot and you didn't answer the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I inform the Trial Chamber about that on Monday? We have scheduled two witnesses who might make it on time but I'm not quite sure. On Monday and Tuesday, we certainly shall have no witnesses. Probably not on Wednesday either but I cannot be sure at this point and I cannot tell you anything more to be -- if I want to be precise and serious. You are always criticising me, Your Honour, saying words are binding and I cannot give you a binding promise at this point. I'm quite aware of that fact. This is actually self criticism because sometimes in the past we scheduled things which then didn't actually occur. That is what I want to avoid, such embarrassment again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, to what day must we postpone now? Do we postpone to Wednesday? Do we postpone to Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until Thursday, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Until Thursday. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are sure it's not standing there, That Wednesday is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is what you should have said ten minutes ago, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it's clear that Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday there will be no court. Just to be clear that, if there is an attempt to change that position on Monday and tell us suddenly that a witness is coming on Wednesday, that's not possible. That's just not possible. We cannot prepare for a witness in two days, so we are going to the bank on the fact that there is not going to be any witnesses. Even if he told us today, it wouldn't be possible. We have been told about one witness next week. We can prepare for one witness and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is exactly as my learned colleague, Mr. Whiting, has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. It's a pity but I do hope that notwithstanding those three days gone, you will still finish on the 20th of November or better still even before. Well, the matter then stands postponed to Thursday, the 9th of November, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II. Thank you. Court adjourned.
